name: Optimize DFlash DDTree TPS on Castle

description: baseline harness failed before benchmark during sync/ssh setup

asi.hypothesis: establish Castle e2e baseline using local-to-remote sync and CUDA harness
asi.rollback_reason: script exited with ssh/rsync code 255 before producing output
asi.next_action_hint: debug autoresearch.sh sync command; likely rsync invoking ssh differently than direct ssh

description: baseline harness failed due shell quoting in remote kill command

asi.hypothesis: fix pkill self-termination in Castle benchmark harness
asi.rollback_reason: bash expanded $1 locally under set -u in the awk kill snippet
asi.next_action_hint: escape awk field as \$1 or avoid awk entirely with pgrep pattern

description: baseline Castle e2e chain-only DDTree benchmark with 1024 target feature window

asi.hypothesis: establish baseline using current stable chain-only exact validation, full target/draft GPU offload, q4 KV, 64k ctx, real rendered prompt
asi.note: committed parser returned 0 likely due regex choosing absent/overwritten field; acceptance parsed from e2e output is the useful commit-rate signal

name: Optimize DFlash DDTree decode TPS on Castle

description: decode-TPS baseline with gen32 after fixing primary metric to exclude prompt/model overhead

asi.hypothesis: use decode-only TPS as the primary metric because current optimization target is per-step decode cost, not prompt prefill/model load
asi.benchmark: Castle e2e gen=32, real_rendered_prompt, 64k ctx, q4 KV, target_feat_ctx=1024
asi.note: committed parser still reports 0 due escaped whitespace regex; output shows committed=33, fix parser next

description: fix committed metric parser; benchmark noise slightly lower than baseline

asi.hypothesis: correct benchmark committed-token parsing without changing runtime code
asi.rollback_reason: primary decode TPS was slightly worse than baseline, likely noise; no runtime optimization tested
asi.next_action_hint: parser fix is in autoresearch.sh and should be preserved as an autoresearch file; proceed to source-level optimization

description: benchmark target feature window 512 for lower draft/pack cost

asi.hypothesis: smaller DFlash target feature context may reduce pack/upload and draft compute enough to improve decode TPS on the real rendered prompt
asi.result: LLAMA_DDTREE_TARGET_FEAT_CTX=512 improved decode TPS from 6.42 to 7.73; pack 8.88->4.49 ms, draft 201.75->171.03 ms, acceptance 1.83->1.94
asi.next_action_hint: confirm 512 on repeated run and test 256/768; if stable, consider default/window recommendation for server workload

description: benchmark target feature window 256 for further draft/pack reduction

asi.hypothesis: target feature context can be reduced below 512 on this prompt without hurting proposal quality, further lowering draft compute and pack cost
asi.result: 256 improved decode TPS to 8.39; draft dropped to 154 ms and pack to 2.24 ms with same acceptance as 512
asi.next_action_hint: test 128 and 384; watch acceptance/regressions because too short a feature window may harm draft quality on broader prompts

description: benchmark target feature window 128

asi.hypothesis: a 128-token target feature window may retain enough recent signal while reducing draft attention and upload cost
asi.result: 128 improved decode TPS to 8.75; draft 144.76 ms, pack 1.09 ms, acceptance unchanged vs 256/512
asi.next_action_hint: test 64 and longer generation/prompt coverage before changing default; risk is hidden acceptance drop on other prompts

description: benchmark target feature window 64; pack lower but draft slower than 128

asi.hypothesis: shrinking target feature window below 128 may further reduce pack and draft context work
asi.rollback_reason: 64 lowered pack to 0.47 ms but draft compute rose to 153 ms and decode TPS fell below the 128-window best
asi.next_action_hint: treat 128 as the current sweet spot on this prompt; test 96/160 only if tuning window further matters

description: benchmark target feature window 96; lower per-step cost lost acceptance

asi.hypothesis: 96-token target feature context might sit between 64 and 128 with lower draft cost but enough proposal quality
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance dropped from 1.94 to 1.74 and required 19 steps; decode TPS below 128-window best
asi.next_action_hint: 128 remains better than smaller windows for this prompt; test 160/192 or move to non-window optimizations

description: benchmark target feature window 160; tied 128 within noise but no improvement

asi.hypothesis: 160-token window may reduce noise versus 128 while keeping acceptance and similar draft cost
asi.rollback_reason: decode TPS was effectively tied but below the 128-window best; no primary improvement
asi.next_action_hint: 128/160 are close; choose 128 for lower memory/pack unless longer prompt validation favors 160

description: benchmark target feature window 192; slower draft than 128/160

asi.hypothesis: 192-token window may retain proposal quality while staying much cheaper than 256/512
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance matched 128 but draft/step time regressed, so primary TPS fell
asi.next_action_hint: do not tune larger windows for this prompt unless broader validation shows 128 harms acceptance

description: default target feature window 128 plus smaller draft context

asi.hypothesis: make 128 the code default and size draft n_ctx to target feature window + block so server avoids oversized draft context
asi.rollback_reason: primary decode TPS was below the prior 128-window env best despite lower set_inputs; draft compute/noise dominated and source change did not improve best
asi.next_action_hint: revisit draft n_ctx sizing separately with repeated runs; the log showed draft n_ctx=256 and set_inputs ~0.7 ms vs ~4 ms, but step time was not better

description: replace small-K heap top-k with fixed array scan

asi.hypothesis: avoid per-row heap allocation/maintenance in extract_top_k_logprobs for K=8 using fixed stack arrays
asi.rollback_reason: topk time increased to 20.98 ms and primary TPS remained below the 128-window best; std heap path is not the bottleneck or is better optimized
asi.next_action_hint: future top-k gains likely need GPU-side logits processing or avoiding logsumexp/scanning, not a small CPU data structure tweak

description: benchmark budget 14 with 128-window; lower top-k cost but no TPS win

asi.hypothesis: budget 14 triggers cheaper K=1/argmax proposal extraction while preserving the same accepted chain on this prompt
asi.rollback_reason: topk dropped 20.8->16.1 ms but total step time did not beat the 128-window budget-22 best; likely draft/noise dominates
asi.next_action_hint: test budget 8/1 only if looking for lower overhead mode; budget 14 is close but not a primary improvement

description: benchmark budget 8 with 128-window; slower than budget 14/22

asi.hypothesis: smaller budget may reduce proposal overhead without reducing accepted chain length in exact-validation mode
asi.rollback_reason: budget 8 had same step count but slower draft/topk aggregate than budget 14 and below best TPS
asi.next_action_hint: budget tuning is not the next major path; keep budget 22 or 14 and focus draft/exact decode

description: confirm 128-window on longer gen request; generation ended at 42 tokens and TPS lower

asi.hypothesis: longer generation should reduce noise and confirm whether 128-window remains best beyond a 32-token sample
asi.rollback_reason: request stopped after 42 generated tokens and acceptance fell to 1.75; decode TPS below current best
asi.next_action_hint: use a non-EOS prompt or different fixture for long-generation confirmation; current rendered prompt is not ideal for 64-token stability

description: change DDTree default target feature window to 128

asi.hypothesis: make the observed 128-token target feature window the default so server/e2e use the faster draft context without requiring an env override
asi.result: default 128 produced the best run so far: 9.11 decode TPS, draft 137.65 ms, pack 1.06 ms, acceptance unchanged at 1.94
asi.next_action_hint: validate on additional prompts before treating 128 as globally safe; env knob still allows raising to 512/1024 if acceptance drops

description: repeat default 128-window run for noise check

asi.hypothesis: re-run the kept 128 default to estimate noise and verify improvement is not a one-off
asi.rollback_reason: repeat was below the 9.11 best but still far above the original 1024-window baseline; no new code changes to keep
asi.next_action_hint: treat 128 default as real but noisy; future comparisons should beat about 8.6-9.1 decode TPS

description: disable DDTree micro-profile logging during benchmark

asi.hypothesis: LLAMA_DDTREE_PROFILE logging may add per-step overhead, so production benchmarking should disable it
asi.rollback_reason: no-profile run did not beat the kept 9.11 TPS best, though it remained above baseline
asi.next_action_hint: keep profiling disabled for user-facing server unless collecting diagnostics; script knob is preserved in autoresearch.sh

description: diagnostic dynamic DDTree block size 8

asi.hypothesis: smaller draft block size may reduce draft/top-k compute enough to offset lower speculative horizon
asi.rollback_reason: block size 8 reduced topk but acceptance dropped and an extra step was needed; primary TPS below current 128-window default
asi.next_action_hint: keep block size 16; reducing block size does not help this prompt

description: benchmark target feature window 32; too little context hurts acceptance

asi.hypothesis: very small target feature window may lower draft compute enough to compensate for weaker proposals
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance dropped to 1.74 and 19 steps were needed, so TPS stayed below the 128 default
asi.next_action_hint: do not go below 128 for this workload unless a broader prompt shows different behavior

description: use K=1 proposal extraction for default exact-validation path

asi.hypothesis: when batched tree verify is disabled, default exact validation can use a top-1 draft chain instead of K=8 tree proposals to reduce top-k overhead while remaining correct
asi.rollback_reason: topk improved by ~3.7 ms but total step time stayed below the 128-window best because draft compute/noise dominated
asi.next_action_hint: K=1 is a possible conservative mode but not a net win in this benchmark; do not keep as default

description: cache DFlash mask token embedding in DDTree driver

asi.hypothesis: avoid per-step mask embedding lookup/allocation when building draft noise embeddings
asi.rollback_reason: change was correct but primary TPS did not beat the 128-window best; mask embedding work is not a measurable bottleneck
asi.next_action_hint: focus on draft graph compute or exact target decode rather than small CPU setup around noise embeddings

description: fast-batched fast-rollback at 128-window still OOMs persist on 64k full-draft

asi.hypothesis: smaller target feature window might free enough memory for fast rollback persist with -ngl65 -ngld6 -c65536
asi.rollback_reason: persist allocation still failed needing 1707.75 MiB; with SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK=0 driver returned empty output
asi.next_action_hint: fast rollback remains nonviable for full-draft 64k on this 24GB GPU unless memory is freed elsewhere; test q4/tq3 or reduced draft offload only if willing to trade draft speed

description: try tq3 KV to fit fast rollback persist; e2e harness does not accept tq3_0

asi.hypothesis: TQ3 KV might free enough VRAM for fast rollback persist with full target/draft offload
asi.rollback_reason: test-speculative-tree-e2e only accepts its hardcoded KV type set and rejected --kv-type tq3_0
asi.next_action_hint: add tq3_0 support to e2e parser before testing this; do not infer runtime viability from this crash

description: add tq3_0 e2e parser support and retry fast rollback; persist still OOMs

asi.hypothesis: with e2e tq3_0 support, smaller KV cache may fit the 1.7 GiB fast rollback persist buffer
asi.rollback_reason: tq3_0 run still failed CUDA persist allocation for 1707.75 MiB and returned empty output with snapshot fallback disabled
asi.next_action_hint: fast rollback requires a larger memory reduction than q4->tq3 KV provides in this harness; avoid more persist-fit tests unless freeing draft layers or compressing persist

description: fast rollback with draft GPU layers 4 still OOMs persist

asi.hypothesis: offloading fewer draft layers may free VRAM for fast rollback persist while retaining enough draft speed
asi.rollback_reason: ngld4 still failed 1707.75 MiB persist allocation and draft time already rose to 280 ms
asi.next_action_hint: if testing persist-fit, drop to ngld3 or lower, but expected draft slowdown likely outweighs rollback savings

description: fast rollback with draft GPU layers 3 fits but is slower than exact path

asi.hypothesis: ngld3 may free enough VRAM for fast rollback and remove exact decode cost
asi.rollback_reason: persist fit and exact cost dropped to zero, but draft slowed to 294 ms and target_tree/rollback path made step 415 ms; TPS far below exact default
asi.next_action_hint: do not trade draft GPU layers for fast rollback on 64k; full draft GPU exact path is better

description: benchmark 32k context for 20k prompt with 128 default

asi.hypothesis: if the prompt fits under 32k, lower target context may reduce memory/compute overhead versus 64k
asi.rollback_reason: 32k context was above baseline but below the 64k 128-window best; no primary improvement in this e2e workload
asi.next_action_hint: context reduction may still help server prefill/memory, but decode step optimization should focus elsewhere

description: benchmark 24k context for 20k prompt

asi.hypothesis: context just above prompt length may reduce decode overhead further than 32k/64k
asi.rollback_reason: decode TPS below current best; smaller n_ctx did not improve step time on this harness
asi.next_action_hint: do not spend more iterations on n_ctx for decode TPS; use n_ctx tuning only for memory/server fit

description: smaller draft context plus full-draft fast rollback still OOMs persist

asi.hypothesis: sizing draft n_ctx to the 128 target-feature window may free enough compute-buffer VRAM for full-draft fast rollback
asi.rollback_reason: fast rollback still failed persist allocation and returned empty output with snapshot fallback disabled
asi.next_action_hint: draft context sizing alone does not free the required 1.7 GiB; persist compression is needed for this route

description: skip exact validation seq_rm diagnostic

asi.hypothesis: default exact chain validation may be clearing an already-empty future range every step; skipping it could save overhead
asi.rollback_reason: correctness passed but primary TPS dropped; seq_rm is not a meaningful bottleneck
asi.next_action_hint: keep the safety clear in exact validation

description: fast-batched with snapshot/replay fallback under 128 default

asi.hypothesis: trusting batched posterior with snapshot fallback might avoid exact decode while preserving correctness
asi.rollback_reason: snapshot/tree/replay path made step time 702 ms, far slower than exact chain default; fast-batched without persist rollback is not viable
asi.next_action_hint: only revisit fast-batched with a no-OOM fast rollback or conditional exact rule; snapshot fallback is too expensive

description: benchmark n_batch 2048 with 512 ubatch

asi.hypothesis: larger prompt batch may improve prefill or reserve behavior without changing decode acceptance
asi.rollback_reason: decode step time worsened; n_batch tuning is not a decode TPS improvement
asi.next_action_hint: keep n_batch=512 for this e2e benchmark unless optimizing prompt prefill separately

description: benchmark n_ubatch 256

asi.hypothesis: smaller ubatch may reduce memory pressure or improve graph reserve for decode
asi.rollback_reason: primary TPS below best and e2e time worsened due slower prompt processing; no decode win
asi.next_action_hint: do not tune ubatch for current decode target

description: print exact validation timing split in e2e harness

asi.hypothesis: surface exact_decode/exact_sample timing in e2e to guide next optimization decisions
asi.rollback_reason: instrumentation did not improve primary TPS and was reverted by experiment rules, though it confirmed exact_decode is essentially all exact cost
asi.next_action_hint: if more diagnostics are needed, re-add exact split intentionally; current useful fact: exact_decode 47.76 ms of exact 48.15 ms

description: benchmark target feature window 112

asi.hypothesis: 112-token window might reduce draft context below 128 without dropping acceptance
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance dropped to 1.83 and an extra step was needed; 128 remains better
asi.next_action_hint: avoid target feature windows below 128 on this prompt

description: benchmark target feature window 144

asi.hypothesis: 144-token window may be a safer slightly larger default than 128 with similar acceptance
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance matched 128 but draft/step time was worse and primary TPS below best
asi.next_action_hint: 128 is still the best target feature default among tested windows

description: tq3_0 KV exact default diverges from chain in e2e

asi.hypothesis: TQ3 KV may reduce memory or improve speed in exact default mode after adding e2e parser support
asi.rollback_reason: correctness failed at first generated token: chain[0]=8635, spec[0]=248069; TQ3 is not a safe drop-in for this correctness gate
asi.next_action_hint: do not use tq3_0 for DDTree correctness until target-only chain/spec equivalence is debugged

description: q8 KV exact default OOMs with full draft at 64k

asi.hypothesis: q8 KV might speed exact decode enough to offset larger memory footprint
asi.rollback_reason: q8_0 KV caused draft context compute buffer allocation OOM with -ngl65 -ngld6 -c65536
asi.next_action_hint: q4_0 remains the viable full-draft 64k KV type on this GPU

description: q8 KV with 32k context fits and nearly matches best

asi.hypothesis: for prompts fitting 32k, q8 KV may fit and speed decode compared with q4 at 64k
asi.rollback_reason: q8_0 + 32k was close but still below the 64k q4 best run, so no primary improvement
asi.next_action_hint: q8_0 + 32k is a viable alternative for <=32k prompts; retest with server/prompt-prefill metric if memory quality matters

description: repeat q8 KV with 32k context

asi.hypothesis: confirm whether q8_0 + 32k close-to-best run was stable
asi.rollback_reason: repeat fell to 8.66 TPS, confirming the 9.05 run was noise/near-best but not better than 64k q4 default
asi.next_action_hint: do not switch primary config to q8_0 + 32k for decode TPS

description: benchmark target feature window 124

asi.hypothesis: 124 may be just below 128 while preserving acceptance
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance preserved but step time was worse than 128 default; no primary improvement
asi.next_action_hint: stop fine-tuning target feature window around 128

description: do not request draft logits for root slot

asi.hypothesis: skip unused root-position draft logits to reduce lm_head/output work by one row per draft step
asi.rollback_reason: correctness remained bit-equal only because exact validation fell back, but draft proposal quality collapsed: acceptance 1.94->1.07 and steps 17->30; logits row indexing/output semantics do not support this simple change
asi.next_action_hint: do not skip root logits without first understanding llama_get_logits_ith output indexing for sparse logits flags

description: suppress root logits flag but keep original logits row indexing

asi.hypothesis: root logits can be disabled while keeping llama_get_logits_ith(1) indexing, reducing output work without changing proposals
asi.rollback_reason: proposal quality stayed intact but draft/topk/step time did not improve enough; primary below best
asi.next_action_hint: root logits flag is not a useful optimization in current llama.cpp output path

description: disable Flash Attention diagnostic with q4 KV

asi.hypothesis: small one-token exact decode and draft attention might be faster without Flash Attention overhead
asi.rollback_reason: q4_0 V cache quantization requires flash_attn, so target context creation failed before benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: only test no-flash with f16 KV if memory allows; q4/q8 quantized V requires Flash Attention

description: no-flash with f16 KV at 32k OOMs target compute buffer

asi.hypothesis: use f16 KV at 32k to allow no-flash attention and test whether one-token decode is faster without Flash Attention
asi.rollback_reason: context creation failed allocating 1739 MiB CUDA compute buffer; no benchmark ran
asi.next_action_hint: no-flash is not viable in current full-offload/full-draft memory envelope; abandon this path

description: force chain recurrent kernel diagnostic

asi.hypothesis: forcing chain recurrent kernels might reduce exact one-token decode overhead or avoid tree-kernel dispatch cost in exact validation
asi.rollback_reason: correctness passed but step time stayed below best; exact remained about 48 ms and topk worsened
asi.next_action_hint: leave chain-kernel force unset for normal runs

description: bulk-copy contiguous spans when packing target feature ring

asi.hypothesis: replace per-column target_feat ring packing with one or two bulk memcpy calls to reduce the remaining pack/upload overhead without changing model behavior
asi.rollback_reason: pack time improved from about 1.06 ms to 0.73 ms, but total step time and primary TPS stayed below the 128-window best; pack is now too small to move throughput alone
asi.next_action_hint: do not spend more iterations on CPU ring packing until larger draft/exact decode bottlenecks are addressed

description: allow DFlash target_feat graph input to reuse draft graph

asi.hypothesis: DFlash draft graph was not reused because target_feat input lacked can_reuse; allowing reuse should stabilize CUDA graph/build and reduce draft overhead without changing math
asi.rollback_reason: graph reuse worked after the first step (reused=1, build_alloc=0) but primary TPS and draft_ms were worse than the 128-window best; graph rebuild cost was not a bottleneck
asi.next_action_hint: do not prioritize graph reuse; focus on actual draft compute (fc/attention/lm_head) or exact target decode

description: fast rollback with budget 14 to reduce persist footprint

asi.hypothesis: lowering DDTree budget from 22 to 14 reduces persist allocation from about 1.7 GiB to about 1.1 GiB and may allow full-draft fast rollback at 64k
asi.rollback_reason: persist allocation still OOMed at 1086.75 MiB; driver produced empty output with snapshot fallback disabled
asi.next_action_hint: full-draft fast rollback needs more than budget reduction; try lower target/draft compute buffers only if expected target_tree cost can still beat exact chain

description: diagnostic larger draft block size 24

asi.hypothesis: increasing DDTree draft block size beyond the trained/default 16 may expose a longer proposal horizon and reduce exact validation steps without changing correctness because exact validation remains authoritative
asi.rollback_reason: block size 24 passed bit-equal correctness but acceptance dropped to 1.79, steps rose to 19, and topk/draft costs increased; primary TPS below best
asi.next_action_hint: do not increase DFlash block size above 16 for this model; the draft quality beyond the default horizon is worse

description: increase DDTree budget to 32 for exact-validation path

asi.hypothesis: larger DDTree budget may include more alternative draft branches so exact chain validation can accept farther before falling off the proposal tree; top-k cost should stay similar because K remains 8
asi.result: budget 32 improved decode TPS to 9.82, reduced steps 17->16, and raised acceptance to 2.06 despite exact_ms rising per step
asi.next_action_hint: confirm with repeat and test budget 40/48; watch for prompt overfit because larger budgets may help only when alternate branches match the exact path

description: test DDTree budget 40 after budget 32 improvement

asi.hypothesis: budget 40 may further improve proposal coverage beyond budget 32 while keeping the same number of exact-validation steps
asi.rollback_reason: acceptance matched budget 32 but step time regressed to 222 ms, especially draft/topk, so primary TPS fell below the budget-32 best
asi.next_action_hint: budget 32 appears better than 40 on this prompt; test budget 28/36 or repeat 32 for noise before changing server defaults further

description: test DDTree budget 28 below budget-32 best

asi.hypothesis: budget 28 may retain the step-count win from budget 32 while reducing tree/proposal overhead
asi.rollback_reason: steps and acceptance matched budget 32, but step time was slower and primary TPS remained below 9.82
asi.next_action_hint: budget 32 remains the best tested budget; test 30/34 or repeat 32 to confirm noise

description: repeat DDTree budget 32 to confirm previous best against noise

asi.hypothesis: repeat budget 32 because the previous 9.82 TPS improvement may include noise; confirm whether the step-count/acceptance gain is stable
asi.rollback_reason: repeat preserved the 16-step and 2.06 acceptance behavior but step time regressed to 222 ms, so primary TPS was below the kept best
asi.next_action_hint: budget 32 still looks structurally useful via fewer steps, but compare future ideas against a noisy 9.0-9.8 TPS range rather than a single best run

description: test DDTree budget 30 between budget 28 and 32

asi.hypothesis: budget 30 may keep the 16-step acceptance gain from budget 32 while trimming proposal overhead versus larger budgets
asi.rollback_reason: budget 30 matched the 16-step/2.06 acceptance pattern but step time stayed around 222 ms and primary TPS remained below the kept budget-32 best
asi.next_action_hint: budget 30/28/40 do not beat budget 32; try budget 34/36 or switch away from budget tuning if repeats remain noisy

description: test DDTree budget 36 above budget-32 best

asi.hypothesis: budget 36 may preserve the 16-step acceptance gain from budget 32 while giving slightly better branch coverage than 30/32 without the overhead seen at 40
asi.rollback_reason: budget 36 passed and was better than 28/30/40, but still below the kept budget-32 best of 9.82 TPS
asi.next_action_hint: budget 34 is the last nearby budget worth testing; otherwise budget tuning appears saturated and noisy around 9.0-9.8 TPS

description: test DDTree budget 34 near budget-32 best

asi.hypothesis: budget 34 may retain the 16-step acceptance improvement from budget 32 while finding a lower-overhead point than 36/40
asi.rollback_reason: budget 34 matched the 16-step and 2.06 acceptance pattern, but topk/step time were worse and primary TPS remained below the kept budget-32 best
asi.next_action_hint: stop local budget sweep around 32; nearby budgets 28/30/34/36/40 all failed to beat 32, so switch to a different bottleneck such as exact target decode or draft compute

description: test budget 32 with target feature window 160

asi.hypothesis: with the larger budget-32 proposal tree, a slightly longer target-feature window may improve draft proposal quality enough to offset extra pack/draft cost
asi.rollback_reason: target_feat_ctx=160 lost the budget-32 structural gain: steps rose from 16 to 17 and acceptance fell to 1.94, so TPS dropped
asi.next_action_hint: keep target feature window at 128 for budget-32; do not combine larger windows with larger budget on this workload

description: test budget 32 with smaller target feature window 112

asi.hypothesis: with budget 32, a smaller 112-token target-feature window may reduce draft compute enough to offset losing some proposal quality
asi.rollback_reason: draft/step time improved significantly, but steps rose to 17 and acceptance fell to 1.94; primary TPS stayed below the kept budget-32 best of 9.82
asi.next_action_hint: try an intermediate window such as 120 with budget 32, or repeat 112 if prioritizing lower draft latency over best TPS

description: test budget 32 with target feature window 120

asi.hypothesis: target_feat_ctx=120 may sit between 112 and 128, retaining some draft-cost savings while avoiding the acceptance loss seen at 112
asi.rollback_reason: 120 did not recover budget-32 acceptance; steps stayed 17 and draft/step time was worse than 112 and 128, so primary TPS fell
asi.next_action_hint: do not continue fine-tuning between 112 and 128; use 128 for structural 16-step behavior or 112 only as lower-latency non-best variant

description: test budget 32 with DDTree micro-profile logging disabled

asi.hypothesis: per-step DDTree micro-profile logging may add overhead in the budget-32 configuration, so disabling it could improve production-like decode TPS
asi.rollback_reason: profile-disabled run preserved the 16-step/2.06 acceptance behavior but did not beat the kept budget-32 best; primary TPS stayed in the noisy ~9.0 band
asi.next_action_hint: profiling can remain disabled in production, but it is not a major optimization lever; move to draft compute or exact decode changes

description: test budget 32 with 32k context and q8 KV

asi.hypothesis: combine the budget-32 branch-coverage gain with the previously viable 32k/q8_0 context to see if q8 exact decode or lower context improves throughput
asi.rollback_reason: q8_0 + 32k lost the budget-32 structural gain: steps rose to 17 and acceptance fell to 1.94, with slower draft/step time
asi.next_action_hint: keep q4_0 64k for budget-32; q8_0/32k does not combine well with this proposal tree

description: test budget 32 with target feature window 116

asi.hypothesis: target_feat_ctx=116 may keep most of the draft-cost reduction seen at 112 while recovering some proposal quality toward the 128-window budget-32 path
asi.rollback_reason: 116 kept lower draft cost but still lost the budget-32 structural win: steps stayed 17 and acceptance stayed 1.94, so primary TPS remained below best
asi.next_action_hint: stop testing sub-128 windows with budget 32; they lower per-step cost but consistently lose the 16-step acceptance behavior

description: test budget 32 with 32k context and q4 KV

asi.hypothesis: for prompts fitting under 32k, lowering n_ctx while keeping q4 KV may reduce decode memory/compute overhead and combine with the budget-32 proposal tree
asi.rollback_reason: 32k context lost the budget-32 structural gain: steps rose to 17 and acceptance fell to 1.94, with TPS well below the 64k budget-32 best
asi.next_action_hint: keep 64k q4 for budget-32 on this workload; context reduction changes proposal/target behavior enough to lose acceptance

description: test budget 32 with target feature window 136

asi.hypothesis: target_feat_ctx=136 may preserve the 16-step budget-32 acceptance behavior while being close enough to 128 to avoid the overhead/regression seen at 160
asi.rollback_reason: 136 preserved the 16-step and 2.06 acceptance behavior, but step time was around 221 ms and primary TPS stayed below the budget-32 best
asi.next_action_hint: 128 remains the best window for budget-32; larger windows preserve acceptance but do not improve throughput

description: test budget 32 with draft top-k capped at 4

asi.hypothesis: budget 32 may not need K=8 alternatives per row; capping draft top-k to 4 could preserve the 16-step acceptance behavior while reducing top-k/tree overhead
asi.rollback_reason: K=4 preserved 16 steps and 2.06 acceptance but primary TPS stayed below the kept budget-32 best; topk did not materially improve
asi.next_action_hint: top-k cardinality is not the main cost; do not add a TOP_K knob unless needed for diagnostics

description: cap DDTree proposal rows to 8 for budget 32

asi.hypothesis: exact-validation path rarely needs all 15 draft rows; capping DDTree proposal rows to 8 may preserve acceptance while reducing CPU top-k scan cost
asi.rollback_reason: topk improved to 17.36 ms and acceptance stayed strong, but exact cost rose and total step time remained below the kept best; also broad prompts could need deeper rows
asi.next_action_hint: tree-row capping can reduce topk but is not enough alone; avoid keeping because it risks hurting prompts with long accepted runs

description: validate budget 32 on longer generation request

asi.hypothesis: longer generation should check whether the budget-32 16-step gain generalizes beyond the short 32-token sample and reduce overfitting risk
asi.rollback_reason: the prompt ended at 42 generated tokens and acceptance fell to 1.83; decode TPS below budget-32 short-run best
asi.next_action_hint: use an additional non-EOS prompt fixture for robust validation; this prompt is useful but not sufficient for long-run budget tuning

description: test pure best-first DDTree without greedy chain seed at budget 32

asi.hypothesis: chain_seed spends many budget-32 nodes on a deep greedy spine even though exact acceptance averages only about 2 tokens; pure best-first may allocate more shallow alternatives and improve proposal coverage
